Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:11:1.hebrew: סד"א מצות הזאה בג' ובז' ואי עבד בחד מנייהו עבד - דרישא דקרא לאו בלישנא דתנאה כתיב, דלא כתיב "אם יתחטא בו", למשמע מיניה: הא אם לא יתחטא לא יטהר, אלא "הוא יתחטא בו", ואיכא למימר: לשון ציווי בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:11:1.english: It might enter your mind to say: The mitzvah of sprinkling [is] on the third and on the seventh, and if he performed [it] on one of them, he has performed [it] - For the beginning of the verse is not written in the phrasing of a condition, as it is not written, “If he purifies himself with it,” so as to imply from it: But if he does not purify himself, he shall not be pure; rather, [it is written,] “He shall purify himself with it,” and it could be said that it is merely the phrasing of a command.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:11:2.hebrew: מחובר - אינו חייב בתרומה, דראשית דגנך כתיב (דברים יח) — מידי דמידגן, שנאסף בכרי. הלכך, לא חל שם תרומה על התלוש שהופרש עליו, וטבל הוא ביד כהן, ויכול לתרום עליה ממקום אחר וכולה חולין. והמחובר שהופרש עליו לא נתקן, ולכשיתלוש צריך לתרום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:11:2.english: Attached - [Produce attached to the ground] is not obligated in teruma, as "the firstfruits of your grain" is written (Deuteronomy 18:4) — [referring to] something that has become grain, which was gathered into a pile. Therefore, the designation of teruma does not take effect on the detached [produce] that was separated for it, and it is tevel in the hand of the priest; and he can separate teruma for it from another place, and all of it is non-sacred [produce]. And the attached [produce] for which it was separated was not rectified, and when he detaches [it], he must separate [teruma].

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:11:3.hebrew: מחובר - אינו חייב בתרומה, דראשית דגנך כתיב (דברים יח) — מידי דמידגן, שנאסף בכרי. הלכך, לא חל שם תרומה על התלוש שהופרש עליו, וטבל הוא ביד כהן, ויכול לתרום עליה ממקום אחר וכולה חולין. והמחובר שהופרש עליו לא נתקן, ולכשיתלוש צריך לתרום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:11:3.english: Attached [produce] - It is not obligated in terumah, for "the first fruit of your grain" is written (Deuteronomy 18:4) — [meaning] an item that becomes grain, which is gathered into a heap. Therefore, the status of terumah does not take effect upon the detached [produce] that was separated for it, and it is tevel in the hand of the priest; and he can separate terumah for it from another place, and all of it is [then] non-sacred produce. And the attached [produce] for which it was separated was not rectified, and when he detaches [it], he must separate terumah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:12:1.hebrew: פירות ערוגה זו מחוברים - כלומר, או שאמר: ״פירות ערוגה זו מחוברים יהיו תרומה כו'״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:12:1.english: The attached produce of this garden bed - That is to say, or [if] he said: “The attached produce of this garden bed shall be teruma...” etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:12:2.hebrew: ונתלשו מהו - שתהא תרומה למפרע — מי הוי כמקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם, או לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:12:2.english: And they were detached, what is [the halakha] - [Does it take effect] so that it is teruma retroactively? Is it considered like one who consecrates something that has not [yet] come into the world, or not?

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:12:3.hebrew: כל שבידו - כי האי, שבידו לתלוש ולהפריש מיד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:12:3.english: Anything that is in one’s power - Such as this [case], where it is in his power to detach [the produce] and separate [the teruma] immediately.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:1:1.hebrew: חרב תאכלו - משמע: אכילתכם הוא חרב, תהיו נשבעים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:1:1.english: “You shall be devoured by the sword” - This implies [that] your food is a sword; you will be sated [with it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:1.hebrew: היינו דכתיב אם לא שכב הנקי - לא כפל: "ואם שכב לא הנקי", אלא מכלל ברכה אתה שומע קללה. דאי משום דסמיך ליה: "ואת כי שטית וגו'", ההוא לא מפרש ביה קללה אשבועה קמייתא, אלא אשבועה דבתריה קאי, דסמיך ליה: "והשביע הכהן את האשה בשבועת האלה", וקמייתא — שבועה שאין בה אלה, דהכי כתיב: "והשביע אותה הכהן וגו'", ולא פי' קללה, אלא מכלל ברכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:1.english: This is [the reason] that it is written: “If no man has lain... you shall be free” - [Scripture] did not double [the condition by stating]: “And if [a man] has lain [with you], you shall not be free”; rather, from the implication of the blessing you deduce the curse. For if [you were to say that the condition was doubled] because it is juxtaposed with: “But if you have gone aside, etc.” (Numbers 5:20), that [verse] does not articulate a curse for the first oath; rather, it refers to the subsequent oath, as juxtaposed to it is: “Then the priest shall charge the woman with the oath of cursing” (Numbers 5:21), whereas the first was an oath that does not contain a curse, for thus it is written: “And the priest shall charge her by oath, etc.” (Numbers 5:19), and it did not specify a curse, but rather [it is derived] from the implication of the blessing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:2.english: But according to Rabbi Meir - It should have [stated]: "And if [a man] has lain [with you], choke!"

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:3.hebrew: היינו דכתיב אם לא שכב הנקי - לא כפל: ״ואם שכב לא הנקי״, אלא מכלל ברכה אתה שומע קללה. דאי משום דסמיך ליה ״ואת כי שטית וגו'״ — ההוא לא מפרש ביה קללה אשבועה קמייתא, אלא אשבועה דבתריה קאי, דסמיך ליה: ״והשביע הכהן את האשה בשבועת האלה״; וקמייתא שבועה שאין בה אלה, דהכי כתיב: ״והשביע אותה הכהן וגו'״, ולא פי' קללה אלא מכלל ברכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:3.english: This is [the reason] that it is written: “If no man has lain... you shall be free” - [Scripture] did not duplicate: “And if [a man] has lain [with you], you shall not be free”; rather, from the implication of the blessing you hear the curse. For if [one were to argue that the condition was duplicated] because juxtaposed to it is: “But if you have gone aside, etc.” — that [verse] does not specify a curse regarding the first oath, but rather pertains to the oath after it, to which is juxtaposed: “Then the priest shall charge the woman with an oath of imprecation”; and the first [oath] was an oath that has no imprecation in it, for so it is written: “And the priest shall charge her with an oath, etc.,” and [Scripture] did not specify a curse, but rather [it is derived] from the implication of the blessing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:4.hebrew: הנקי כתיב - בלא יוד, למידרשיה כמקראו לשבועה ראשונה: ״אם לא שכב״ — תהא נקייה; ובמסורת נמי מידריש אשבועה קמייתא, למישדייה אקרא דבתריה ולמימר: ״חנקי, ואת כי שטית״ — כלומר: אם שטית, תתחנקי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:2:4.english: “Hinnaki” is written - [It is written] without a yod, so that it may be expounded according to its reading for the first oath: “If [a man] has not lain [with you]” — she shall be cleared; and according to the Masorah, it is also expounded regarding the first oath, to attach it to the subsequent verse and say: “Choke [ḥinnaki], and you, if you have gone aside” — that is to say: If you have gone aside, you shall choke.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:3:1.hebrew: אלא לרבי חנינא - דלא בעי כפילה, למה לי למיכתב כי האי לישנא, ואיכא למידרשיה הכי והכי? נכתוב "תחיה" או לשון אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:3:1.english: But according to Rabbi Ḥanina - Since he does not require a duplicated [condition], why do I need [the verse] to write in this phrasing, such that it can be expounded this way and that way? Let it write "you shall live" or another phrasing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:5:1.hebrew: סד"א מצות הזאה בג' ובז' ואי עבד בחד מנייהו עבד - דרישא דקרא לאו בלישנא דתנאה כתיב, דלא כתיב "אם יתחטא בו", למשמע מיניה: הא אם לא יתחטא — לא יטהר, אלא "הוא יתחטא בו", ואיכא למימר: לשון ציווי בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:5:1.english: It might enter your mind to say: The mitzvah of sprinkling [is] on the third and on the seventh, and if he performed [it] on one of them he has performed [it] - For the beginning of the verse is not written in conditional phrasing, as it is not written: "If he purifies himself with it," [from which] to deduce: behold, if he does not purify himself, he will not become pure; rather, "He shall purify himself with it," and it can be said [that] it is merely phrasing of a command.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:6:1.hebrew: והזה הטהור על הטמא וגו' למה לי - לאו לרבי חנינא פריך, אלא לדברי הכל בעי לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:6:1.english: And the pure shall sprinkle on the impure, etc., why do I [need this] - [The Gemara] is not objecting according to Rabbi Ḥanina, but rather according to everyone it asks this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:6:2.english: To exclude the sixth [day] - For he did not distance the sprinkling from his impurity.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:6:3.hebrew: ה"ג אבל היכא דעבד בשלישי ובשמיני דקא מפיש בימי טהרה אימא שפיר דמי - ולא גריס ברביעי ובשמיני, דהא ודאי שפיר דמי, דכל מה שמשהה הזאה ראשונה אין בכך כלום, ובלבד שלא ירבה ושלא ימעט בימים שבין הזאה להזאה, כדאמר גבי כהן הפורש שבעה לפני יום הכפורים (יומא דף ח:): בשלמא ראשון שמא שלישי, שני שמא שלישי — ואע"ג דאיכא לספוקי נמי שמא עשירי או יותר הוא. ואי גרסי' הכי, לענין מצות הזאה בזמנה הוא דגרסינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:6:3.english: This is the reading: “However, where he performed [it] on the third and on the eighth, in which case he increases the days of purity, say [that this] is proper” - And one should not read: “[where he performed it] on the fourth and on the eighth,” for that is certainly valid, as however much one delays the first sprinkling, there is nothing [disqualifying] in this, provided that one neither increases nor decreases the days between one sprinkling and the other. As [the Gemara] says regarding the [High] Priest who separates [for] seven [days] before Yom Kippur (Yoma 8b): “Granted, [on the] first [day, he is sprinkled lest it be the] third [day]; [on the] second [day, lest it be the] third [day],” and even though there is [reason] to be doubtful also that perhaps it is the tenth [day] or more. And if one reads this [version], it is regarding the mitzvah of sprinkling in its [proper] time that we read it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:6:4.english: For he increases the days of purity - He moves further away from the day of contact with the impurity.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:8:1.hebrew: שלא הטעתו - אלא הוא הטעה את עצמו, וכיון דלא פירש — לאו כל כמיניה, דהוו להו דברים שבלב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:8:1.english: That she did not mislead him - Rather, he misled himself; and since he did not state [his condition] explicitly, it is not in his power [to annul the betrothal], as they are [merely] matters of the heart.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:8:2.hebrew: שלא הטעתו - אלא הוא הטעה את עצמו, וכיון דלא פירש, לאו כל כמיניה, דהוו להו דברים שבלב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:8:2.english: Because she did not mislead him - Rather, he misled himself; and since he did not make [his condition] explicit, it is not in his power [to void the betrothal], for they are [merely] matters of the heart [which carry no legal weight].

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:9:1.hebrew: לאחר שיחלוץ ליך יבמיך - קסבר האי תנא, אין קידושין תופסין ביבמה לשוק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:9:1.english: After your yavam performs chalitzah for you - This Tanna holds that betrothal does not take effect upon a yevamah with an outsider.

Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:9:2.hebrew: אינה מקודשת - דהוה ליה דברים שלא באו לעולם, ועכשיו אין בידו לקדשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 62a:9:2.english: She is not betrothed - For it has the status of things that have not come into the world, and currently it is not in his power to betroth her.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:11:1.hebrew: ת"י: בשלמא לר"מ היינו דכתיב הוא יתחטא וגו' ואם לא יתחטא - תימה: מה ענין זה למחלוקת? אפילו לר"מ, למה לי? והלא בהרבה מקומות כתיב (ויקרא יד) "ורחץ במים וטהר", ולא הוצרך לומר "ואם לא ירחץ לא יטהר"! וי"ל דלא דמי: דהתם מילתא דפשיטא, כיון דמצוה הוא שצוה הקב"ה — אם לא עשה, לא יצא; אבל הכא משמע קצת שהוא לשון תנאי, מדכתיב "הוא יתחטא", והוי כאילו כתיב "אם יתחטא בו יטהר", ולא כתיב "ויתחטא ויטהר" — ואז הוי ציווי, כמו "ורחץ וטהר":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:11:1.english: [Tosafot Yeshanim:] "Granted, according to Rabbi Meir, this is that which is written: 'He shall purify himself...' etc., 'and if he does not purify himself'" - It is astonishing: What does this matter have to do with the dispute? Even according to Rabbi Meir, why do I need [the verse to state the negative]? For is it not written in many places (Leviticus 14): "And he shall wash in water and be pure", and it was not necessary [for the verse] to state: "And if he does not wash, he will not be pure"?! And one can say that it is not comparable: For there it is an obvious matter: since it is a mitzvah that the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded, if one did not perform it, he has not fulfilled [his obligation]; but here, it implies somewhat that it is the phrasing of a condition, since it is written: "He shall purify himself", and it is as though it is written: "If he purifies himself with it, he shall be pure" — and it is not written: "And he shall purify himself and be pure", which would then have been a command, like "and he shall wash and be pure".

Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:11:2.hebrew: אין תורמין מן התלוש על המחובר - פי' בקונטרס: המחובר אינו חייב בתרומה, דכתיב (דברים יח): "ראשית דגנך", דבעינן מידי דמידגן; וא"כ, הוי מן החיוב על הפטור. וקשה: דאם כן, לדבריו, בתלוש נמי קודם שנתמרח לא הוי תרומה, שהרי לא מידגן! וליתא, דהא אמר בעלמא (עירובין דף לא:): "מעשר ראשון שהקדימו בשבולים פטור מתרומה גדולה", דמשמע דמהני. וע"ק מההיא דאמר (תרומות פ"א מ"י): "התורם מדבר שנגמר מלאכתו" — דהיינו אחר מירוח — "על דבר שלא נגמרה מלאכתו" — והיינו קודם מירוח — "תרומתו תרומה". לכ"נ לר"י: הא דמחובר פטור — נפקא לן מדכתיב "ממנו", דדריש בספרי: "'ממנו' — ולא מן המחובר", דהא קרא בתלוש מיירי; וע"כ אתא למימר: "ממנו" — אפילו בדיעבד נמי אסור; דאי משום לכתחילה אתא — תיפוק לי משום דכתיב "דגנך", ומחובר לאו מידגן הוא. אלא שמע מינה דפסול אפילו בדיעבד במחובר; וההיא דמעשר שהקדימו בשבולים דמהני בדיעבד — מיירי בתלוש וקודם מירוח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:11:2.english: One may not separate terumah from detached [produce] for attached [produce] - Rashi explains in the Kuntres: Attached [produce] is not obligated in terumah, as it is written (Deuteronomy 18:4): "The first fruits of your grain," for we require an item that is processed into grain [midegan]; and if so, it is [separating] from that which is obligated for that which is exempt. And this is difficult: For if so, according to his words, in [the case of] detached [produce] as well before it was smoothed [into a pile], it should not be [valid] terumah, as it is not [yet] grain! And this is not so, for [the Gemara] says elsewhere (Eruvin 31b): "First tithe that one separated early, [while it was still] in the stalks, is exempt from great terumah" — which implies that it is effective. And furthermore, [it is] difficult from that which is stated (Terumot 1:10): "One who separates terumah from an item whose work is completed" — that is, after smoothing — "for an item whose work is not completed" — and that is, before smoothing — "his terumah is [valid] terumah." Therefore, it appears to the Ri: This [rule] that attached [produce] is exempt is derived by us from that which is written: "From it" [Numbers 18:26], which is expounded in the Sifrei: "'From it' — and not from that which is attached," for this verse is dealing with detached [produce]; and perforce it comes to state: "From it" [means that] even after the fact it is also forbidden. For if it came [only to teach that it is forbidden] ab initio, let it be derived from that which is written: "Your grain," as attached [produce] is not grain. Rather, learn from this that it is invalid even after the fact in [the case of] attached [produce]. And that [case] of tithe that one separated early, [while still] in the stalks, which is effective after the fact, is dealing with [produce that is] detached and before smoothing.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:2:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרבי חנינא בן גמליאל היינו דכתיב אם לא שכב הנקי - פירש בקונטרס: שלא כפל "אם שכב לא הנקי", אלא מכלל ברכה אתה שומע קללה. דאי משום דסמיך ליה "ואת כי שטית וגו'", ההיא לא מפרש ביה קללה אשבועה קמייתא, אלא אשבועה בתרייתא קאי, דסמיך ליה: "והשביע הכהן את האשה בשבועת האלה וגו'"; ושבועה קמייתא אין בה אלה, דהכי כתיב: "והשביע אותה הכהן", ולא פירש בה קללה אלא מכלל ברכה. וקשה: דהא כל תנאי מבני גד ומבני ראובן גמרי', וא"כ בעינן הן קודם ללאו, והכא הוה לאו קודם להן, דהא "אם לא שכב" כתיב ברישא! וי"ל: ד"אם לא שכב" חשוב הן, שמה שאנו רוצים שתעשה חשוב הן, דומיא ד"אם יעברו" — שאנו רוצים שיעברו, ואם לא יעברו יפסידו; כך אנו רוצים שתתקיים דברים שלא שכב איש אותה, וזהו הן, ואם שכב תפסיד, וזהו לאו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:2:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel, this is why it is written: "If no man has lain [with you]... you shall be free" - Rashi explained: That [the Torah] did not double [the condition by stating]: "If [a man] has lain, you shall not be free"; rather, from the implication of the blessing you infer the curse. For if [one were to suggest that the condition was doubled] because adjacent to it is [written]: "And you, if you have gone astray, etc." — that [verse] does not specify a curse for the first oath; rather, it refers to the second oath, which is adjacent to it: "Then the priest shall adjure the woman with an oath of cursing, etc." And the first oath contains no curse, for so it is written: "And the priest shall adjure her," and it did not specify a curse in it, but rather [the curse is inferred] from the implication of the blessing. And [this] is difficult: For behold, all [rules of] conditions we derive from [the condition of] the children of Gad and the children of Reuven, and if so, we require that the affirmative precede the negative! Yet here, the negative preceded the affirmative, for behold, "If [a man] has not lain" is written first! And one can say: "If [a man] has not lain" is considered the affirmative, because that which we desire to happen is considered the affirmative, similar to "If they cross over" — where we desire that they cross over, and if they do not cross over they lose [their land]. So too, we desire that the matter be fulfilled that no man has lain with her, and that is the affirmative; and if [a man] has lain, she loses, and that is the negative.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:2:3.hebrew: הנקי - כתיב. פירש בקונטרס: והכי כופל: ואם לא שכב — הנקי, ואם שכב — "חנקי ואת כי שטית", דקאי "חנקי" א"ואת כי שטית" דכתיב בתריה. וקשה: דא"כ, הוה ליה מעשה קודם לתנאי; ואנן אמרינן במתני' דר"מ בעי תנאי קודם למעשה! לכן פר"י: דלא קאי כלל א"ואת כי שטית" דכתיב בתריה, אלא כתיב "הנקי", והוי כאילו היה כתיב "חנקי", והכהן היה חוזר וכופל: "אם שכב — חנקי"; והשתא הוי תנאי קודם למעשה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:2:3.english: Hinnaki - [is] written. Rashi explained: And this is how he doubles [the condition]: "If [no man] has lain [with you] — you shall be free [hinnaki]; and if [a man] has lain [with you] — 'you shall choke, and you, if you have gone astray' [ḥinnaki ve'at ki satit]," as [the word] "ḥinnaki" refers to "and you, if you have gone astray" which is written after it. And this is difficult: for if so, this is [a case of] the action preceding the condition; and we say in the Mishnah that Rabbi Meir requires the condition to precede the action! Therefore, the Ri explained: it does not refer at all to "and you, if you have gone astray" which is written after it; rather, "hinnaki" is written, and it is as though "ḥinnaki" were written, and the priest would reiterate and double [the condition]: "If [a man] has lain [with you] — you shall choke [ḥinnaki]!" And now, the condition precedes the action.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:2:4.hebrew: [חנקי כתיב - פי' ר"ח דה"ק: "אם לא שכב וגו' תחת אישך" — כלומר: תשאר תחת אישך; "ואת כי שטית וגו' מבלעדי אישך" — כלומר: תלכי ממנו; והוי תנאי קודם למעשה. ואע"ג דהוי לאו קודם להן — הא אמרינן מהכא (סנהדרין לב: לג.): "פותחין בזכות תחילה"]: ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:2:4.english: [“Ḥinnaki is written” - Rabbeinu Chananel explained that this is what [the verse] means: “If no man has lain [with you...], under your husband” — that is, you shall remain under your husband; “and you, if you have gone astray [...], away from your husband” — that is, you shall depart from him. And [thus] the condition precedes the act. And even though the negative [clause] precedes the positive [clause], behold, we say from here (Sanhedrin 32b–33a): “One opens with acquittal first.”]: Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:4:1.hebrew: בשלמא לר"מ היינו דכתיב הוא יתחטא וגו' ואם לא יתחטא - תימה: מה ענין זה למחלוקת? אפילו לר"מ למה לי? והלא בהרבה מקומות כתיב (ויקרא י״ד:ח׳): "ורחץ במים וטהר", ולא הוצרך לומר: "ואם לא ירחץ לא יטהר"! וי"ל, דלא דמי; דהתם מילתא דפשיטא, כיון דמצוה הוא שצוה הקב"ה — אם לא עשה לא יצא; אבל הכא משמע קצת שהוא לשון תנאי, מדכתיב "הוא יתחטא", והוי כאילו כתיב "אם יתחטא בו יטהר", ולא כתיב "ויתחטא ויטהר" ואז הוי ציווי כמו "ורחץ וטהר":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 62a:4:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir, this is why it is written: “He shall purify himself... but if he does not purify himself” - It is puzzling: What does this matter have to do with the dispute? Even according to Rabbi Meir, why do I need [this clause]? Behold, in many places it is written: “And he shall wash in water and be pure” (Leviticus 14:8), and [the Torah] did not need to state: “and if he does not wash, he shall not be pure”! And it can be answered that it is not comparable: For there, it is an obvious matter: since it is a mitzvah that the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded, if he did not perform [it], he did not fulfill [his obligation]. But here, it implies somewhat that it is the phrasing of a condition, since it is written: “He shall purify himself,” which is as if it were written: “If he purifies himself with it, he shall be pure”; and it is not written: “And he shall purify himself and be pure,” which would then have been a command like “and he shall wash and be pure.”
